subject: FinLytics performance SLOs - p95/p99 latency qualification (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@finlytics.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps - perf SLOs (p95/p99)

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Great to meet earlier - thanks for walking us through the FinLytics latency goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Summary of requirements from the call:
- End-to-end p95 target: <= 250 ms
- End-to-end p99 target: <= 600 ms
- Typical request: ~600 input tokens, ~80 output tokens on average (few longer generations up to ~1k output tokens)
- Concurrency baseline: 8-16 concurrent inferences per region; burst to 80+ for short periods
- Streaming support: yes, you rely on token-by-token streaming for UI responsiveness and partial scoring
- SLA needs: hosted API ideally, but must validate parity vs your current provider on latency and tail behavior

What we heard about current provider performance (please confirm):
- Current provider p95: ~450 ms end-to-end (varies by model and region)
- Current provider p99: ~1.1-1.4 s (tail spikes during bursts)

Proposed mutual action plan:
1) You share a small sample set of real prompts + avg token sizes and a representative RPS pattern (or traces) - we can use these to drive a synthetic load test.
2) We run a hosted evaluation in us-west with the same model config and report p50/p95/p99, plus streaming-first-byte times and token-stream latency.
3) SE (Aditya) will provide a short runbook for the replay so your infra team can reproduce locally if desired.
4) Quick 30-45m follow-up next week to review traces and decide next steps (Dedicated or Hosted).

I've attached a short SLO deck that outlines how we measure end-to-end latency (redwood-slo-deck.pdf).

Next steps for you: share sample traces or a 1-page RPS/traffic profile and confirm which model(s) you want us to test.

Thanks -
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178
From: Sarah Green <sarah.green@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - perf SLOs (p95/p99)

Thanks Marissa - this is great, and matches what we discussed. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Model: currently using a 70B open-weights model (quantized) - prefer Redwood to test with the same checkpoint if possible.
- Average payload: our UI sends 2-3 partial prompts in quick succession; effective per-request token counts are ~700 tokens combined (input+output).
- Concurrency: baseline for our EU+US customers is ~12 concurrent; we see short bursts up to ~120 concurrent during market open.
- Streaming: critical. If streaming introduces additional per-token overhead vs non-streamed responses that affects p95, that's a blocker for our UX.

Attached a small sample trace file (finlytics-sample-traces.jsonl) with 50 anonymized requests and a short traffic profile.

Can you confirm the exact metrics you'll report back? We want raw p50/p95/p99, initial response time (time-to-first-byte/token), and token-streaming latency distribution. Also please include the test harness config (threads, batch sizes, concurrency) you used.

Happy to jump on the follow-up after you run the eval - are you available next Tue 10-10:45am PT?

- Sarah
Head of Product | FinLytics
sarah.green@finlytics.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - perf SLOs (p95/p99)

Thanks Sarah - got the traces, very helpful. Quick technical notes and what we'll run: 

1) Test plan we will execute (hosted-us-west):
   - Model: same 70B checkpoint (quantized config) per your request.
   - Workload: replay of the 50 requests + synthetic ramp to emulate your burst profile (baseline 12 concurrency -> 120 burst).
   - Metrics: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, TTFB (first token), per-token streaming latency percentiles, max concurrency observed, and CPU/GPU utilization.
   - Batch policy: we'll test both 1) server-side batching disabled and 2) adaptive batching with latency SLO = 250 ms to show tradeoffs.

2) What we'd like from FinLytics (if available):
   - A sample API key we can use for test replay (or we can replay against your staging endpoint if you prefer).
   - Confirmation of typical allowed max latency for non-streamed responses (if different from streamed).

3) Deliverables from Redwood:
   - Raw CSV/JSON of per-request latencies and traces (we'll include request ids that map back to your sample traces).
   - A short write-up comparing hosted-vs-current-provider with visualizations (tail-latency CDFs).

I've attached the small SLO deck Marissa referenced (redwood-slo-deck.pdf) and will kick off the hosted run once you confirm model/checkpoint and share an API key or allow replay access.

I'll also include a short smoke test we recommend you run locally so results are comparable.

- Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Green <sarah.green@finlytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps - perf SLOs (p95/p99)

Perfect - thanks Aditya and Sarah.

Sarah: Tue 10-10:45am PT works for us. I've penciled in a 30-minute slot and included the calendar link here: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=finlytics-slo-review

Action items (owner / due):
- FinLytics: share API key or enable staging replay + confirm model checkpoint (Sarah) / by EOD Thu 8/6
- Redwood (Aditya): run hosted eval (us-west) + share raw traces + write-up / by EOD Mon 8/10
- Marissa: compile results and schedule 30m review (me) / by Tue 8/11

If we see parity (p95/p99 within your targets and streaming-first-byte acceptable) we can scope Dedicated sizing or discuss reserved capacity options. Looking forward to it.

Thanks!
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
--
Thread notes: internal participants limited to Redwood employees listed in agents.md. Attachments: redwood-slo-deck.pdf (SLO measurement details), finlytics-sample-traces.jsonl (anonymized request traces).
